supersedes: modern/spec/pic2d/pic2d-model-v2.0.json (v2.0.6) and pic2d-model-v2.1.json: every v2.0.6 / v2.1 physics, gate, time-step, checkpoint and artifact contract is kept; this file adds ONE optional physics block, secondary electron emission from the dielectric wall (audit gap (a), roadmap R2). A configuration without the block (PIC2DConfig.see = None) is bit-identical to v2.0.6 in configuration identity, dynamics, ledger keys, window sums, maps and frames (test_pic2d_v22_see.py::test_see_off_reproduces_the_v2_0_6_identity_ledger_and_tallies; whole-state comparison against the 0901138a tree made offline on cpu and warp-cpu: particles, phi, surface charge, cumulative ledger, maps bitwise).
status: implemented-2026-09-05-development-screening-verified-numerics-not-validated-physics; no campaign preregistered (the coordinator schedules the R2 runs after R1)
source_of_the_changes: modern/docs/pic2d-physics-completeness-audit.md (0901138a) sections 4.a (SEE) and 4.b (dielectric surface charge), roadmap R2; references verified through their DOIs on 2026-09-05 (see see_dielectric_v1.references)
what_changed: physics: electron impacts on the dielectric wall (boundary code 3; channel walls, cone stair-steps, the dielectric flange of a plume geometry's front face) emit an integer number of macro-electrons of the impacting macro weight sampled without bias from the energy- and angle-dependent total yield delta(E, theta) - Vaughan 1989/1993 curve with per-material constants plus the Sydorenko 2006 three-component split (elastic / inelastic backscatter / true secondaries) and optional low-energy elastic bump; ion impacts emit with a constant ion-induced yield (default 0)

wall: the accumulated surface charge on the plasma-side wall nodes (present since v1.0: finite-volume Gauss law with the surface charge as a RHS source on the floating Neumann dielectric) now changes by absorbed MINUS emitted charge, (-1 + n) e W per electron impact and (+1 + n_i) e W per ion impact, deposited with the same renormalised bilinear weights as the absorbed charge (exact fixed-point integer multiples); anode / exit / far-field / body-conductor Dirichlet surfaces are unaffected and the grounded front-face conductor does not emit

ledger: the emitted kinetic energy is an INJECTED term (ke_see_emitted_j; the impact energy stays in ke_absorbed_wall_j), the emitted axial momentum enters the momentum ledger (pz_see_emitted; net wall momentum = absorbed - emitted); counts see_impacts / see_electrons / see_ion_induced_electrons / see_backscattered / see_yield_sum / see_yield_clamped - all EXTRA ledger keys, present only when the wall emits; the particle-side identity dKE = field work + injected - absorbed + born - W(n E)e + emitted closes to round-off on cpu / warp-cpu / cuda and the electron count identity gains the emitted term

diagnostics: series record gains ledger.interval_see_emitted_j, currents_a.see_emission_a / see_effective_yield and a see block (interval / cumulative effective yield, mean yield, clamped impacts, emission current, backscattered fraction, mean emitted energy, emitted power, wall potential mean / min / max, plasma-minus-wall drop, the Hobbs-Wesson critical yield and an at_or_above flag); window sums gain wall_see_electrons / wall_see_energy_j per axial wall cell -> maps and frames gain wall_see_flux_per_m2_s, wall_see_effective_yield (emitted / impacting per cell: the per-cusp regime diagnostic) and wall_see_mean_energy_ev (additive; absent without SEE); the runner's series arrays gain see_* columns and the current_see_* columns

backends: CPU reference (see.py emit_secondaries, appended to the population after MCC and injection) and Warp (warp_see.py: push_kernel flags the impact slot, an end-of-step stage reconstructs the impact from the retained pre-push state, samples, scans and spawns; graph-capturable; 4th per-step RNG stream); Warp device reservation see_birth_bound = 256 + N_e / 1000 slots per step, overflow fails closed at the sync

identity: SEEConfig.to_dict (model name, every field, the resolved material constants with their provenance strings, the emission contract) enters config_sha256 whenever PIC2DConfig.see is set; see = None leaves every recorded identity unchanged; the runner reads numerics.see
scaffold retired: the v1.4 SEEConfig that refused enabled = True is replaced (sensitivity.SEEConfig re-exports see.SEEConfig; virtual_wall_yield stays as the map diagnostic)

see_dielectric_v1.config: PIC2DConfig.see = SEEConfig(enabled=True, material='BN'|'Al2O3', yield_model='vaughan_components'|'constant', constant_yield, constant_yield_threshold_ev, emission_temperature_ev=2.0, ion_induced_yield=0.0, max_emitted_per_impact=8, space_charge_limit_yield=0.983, overrides={material constant: value}); runner key numerics.see with the same fields

yield_model.total: delta_V(E, theta) = delta_max(theta) (v e^(1-v))^k, v = (E - E_0)/(E_max(theta) - E_0), k = k_rise (v < 1), 0.25 (1 <= v <= 3.6), 1.125 / v^0.35 tail (v > 3.6), E_max(theta) = E_max (1 + k_s theta^2 / 2 pi), delta_max(theta) = delta_max (1 + k_s theta^2 / pi) [Vaughan 1989, 1993; k_s = 1], plus the optional low-energy elastic bump gamma_e,max b(E) with b = v_1 e^(1 - v_1) below its peak and (1 + v_2) e^(-v_2) above it [Sydorenko 2006 thesis eq. 3.16]
yield_model.components: elastic r_e delta_V + bump (impact speed kept), inelastic r_i delta_V (energy uniform in (0, E)), true (1 - r_e - r_i) delta_V (flux half-Maxwellian at T_see: normal Rayleigh + tangential Gaussian -> energy E e^(-E/T)/T^2, mean 2 T_see, cosine angular law); r_e = 0.03, r_i = 0.07 [Sydorenko 2006 thesis eqs 3.16-3.18, BN]; each emitted electron is one component drawn with probability proportional to its partial yield
yield_model.integer_yield: n = floor(delta) + Bernoulli(delta - floor(delta)) per impact (E[n] = delta), clamped at max_emitted_per_impact (clamped impacts tallied); the emitted macro weight equals the impacting macro weight
yield_model.angle_of_incidence: theta = arccos(|v_n| / |v|) with v_n the velocity component along the crossed face's normal
yield_model.emission_point: the impact segment (pre-push -> post-push position, linearly interpolated in (r, z)) crossing of the last plasma cell's face - the first face crossed unless the cell behind it is plasma, then the second (the Courant limit allows one diagonal cell change) - nudged 1e-6 cell into the plasma cell, tangential coordinate clamped into that cell; emitted electrons start at the wall potential and are pushed from the next step
yield_model.angular_emission: cosine law about the inward normal of the crossed face (cos theta_2 = sqrt(u)) for the backscattered components; the true-secondary sampler yields the cosine law by construction [Sydorenko 2006 eq. 3.20: isotropic in azimuth, cosine in polar angle, independent of the incidence angle]
yield_model.ion_induced: constant yield gamma_i (default 0; Xe+ on ceramics 0.01-0.1 at 100-400 eV per the audit's 4.h estimate), true secondaries at T_see, tallied separately
yield_model.space_charge_limit: NOT imposed: the emitted electrons are ordinary macro-electrons, so when the local yield exceeds the Hobbs-Wesson limit the sheath goes non-monotonic and returns the excess to the wall (re-absorbed at their emission energy: BN yield 0.14 at 1 eV, so no breeding); the effective (wall-defined) yield emitted/impacting and the wall potential are recorded per interval and per wall cell so the regime is diagnosable; space_charge_limit_yield (0.983 = 1 - 8.3 sqrt(m_e/M) for xenon) is a diagnostic threshold only

BN.source: Vaughan fit of the total electron emission yield of boron nitride measured by Villemant, Belhaj, Sarrailh, Dadouch, Garrigues and Boniface 2019 (EPL 127, 23001, doi:10.1209/0295-5075/127/23001; 10-1000 eV) as tabulated by the PICLas code (SEE model 13 coefficients a 2.016, b 299 eV, c 0.563, W 0)
BN.consistency_checks: first crossover 35.7 eV vs Dunaevsky, Raitses and Fisch 2003 (Phys. Plasmas 10, 2574, doi:10.1063/1.1568344) Table 1 power-fit E_1 = 35 eV for BN grade HP (their linear fit: 40 eV); delta(10 eV) = 0.51 vs their linear-fit sigma_0 = 0.54; Maxwellian-flux-averaged yield 0.48 / 0.58 / 0.69 / 0.98 at T_e 5 / 7 / 10 / 20 eV; critical temperature (flux average = 0.983) 20.3 eV vs 19.3 eV from the Dunaevsky linear fit (Goebel-Katz form) and 18.3 eV in Sydorenko 2006 - pinned by test_material_constants_reproduce_the_cited_anchors_and_the_identity_carries_them
BN.note: the audit's provisional set (delta_max 2.9 at 350 eV, threshold 12.5 eV; flux-averaged 0.28 at 7 eV) is superseded: the Villemant fit with a zero threshold carries the low-energy elastic floor that every dielectric shows (Dunaevsky 2003 section IV), so the 7 eV flux-averaged yield is 0.58, not 0.28 - the predeclared hypotheses below keep the audit's directions with this larger yield

Al2O3.source: DECLARED, not digitised: maximum 6.4 at 650 eV from the Dawson 1966 (J. Appl. Phys. 37, 3644, doi:10.1063/1.1708934) alumina range 5-7 at 450-700 eV as compiled by the USU / Dennison electron-yield work; Vaughan 1993 (IEEE Trans. Electron Devices 40, 830, doi:10.1109/16.202798) threshold 12.5 eV and k 0.56; low-energy elastic bump gamma_e,max 0.5 at 5-10 eV per Sydorenko 2006 thesis eq. 3.16 (peak 7.5 eV, decay 10 eV declared)
Al2O3.consistency_checks: first crossover 16.0 eV; flux-averaged yield 0.63 / 0.82 / 1.09 at 5 / 7 / 10 eV; critical temperature 8.7 eV - the more emissive wall at every plateau temperature, as the audit's 'Al2O3 > BN in every effect' requires
Al2O3.caveat: Tondu, Belhaj and Inguimbert 2011 (J. Appl. Phys. 110, 093301, doi:10.1063/1.3653820) report the Al2O3 yield FALLING with electron exposure (and BN's rising), so this set is a sensitivity bracket, not a measurement of the flight ceramic; digitising their curves is the open item

see_dielectric_v1.identity_policy: SEE parameters enter config_sha256 through SEEConfig.to_dict whenever PIC2DConfig.see is set (including enabled = False, which records the block without emission); see = None is the v2.0.6 identity. Material presets are named; any override is listed explicitly in the identity with its value. A different material, yield model, emission temperature, ion-induced yield, cap or override is a different configuration.

ledger.energy: sources = injected - absorbed(anode, exit, wall) - W(n_exc E_exc + n_ion E_ion) e + born + electrode work + ke_see_emitted; recorded residual = H (numerical energy creation) exactly as v2.0.6; identity test closes to <= 1e-6 of the kinetic-energy scale (round-off level) on cpu / warp-cpu / cuda with SEE on, and fails by the whole emitted power without the emitted term
ledger.particles: N_e(t) = seed + injected + ionisations + see_electrons + see_ion_induced_electrons - absorbed(anode, exit, wall) exactly (host bookkeeping and device compaction agree at every sync)
ledger.surface_charge: sum(surface) = e W (wall_ions - wall_electrons + see_electrons + see_ion_induced_electrons) to the fixed-point unit 2^-40 e W per contribution
ledger.momentum: pz_see_emitted is a source; absorbed wall momentum is reported net of it; the interval momentum ledger stays round-off

diagnostics.wall_nodes_for_the_potential_diagnostic: stair-step wall nodes plus the unknown nodes of the outer grid row (a straight bore's wall lies on the outer grid line, which the mesh's 'adjacent to a solid cell' wall flag does not mark)
diagnostics.per_cusp: the closure extraction (pic2d_design_mini_sweep_v1/closure.py cusp windows) applies unchanged to the new profiles: per-cusp SEE current = e x sum over the cusp window of wall_see_flux x wall area; per-cusp effective yield = its ratio to the cusp electron wall current

predeclared_hypotheses_from_the_audit.reference: audit section 4.a / table 3 row (a) / roadmap R2 on the accepted 33 um ss-v4 plateau 0d228ad2 (SEE off) vs the same protocol with SEE on: BN and Al2O3
predeclared_hypotheses_from_the_audit.wall_electron_power: UP x1.5-2 (the lower sheath admits more primaries; the emitted flux returns part of the energy at T_see)
predeclared_hypotheses_from_the_audit.discharge_current: UP 10-30 % (more electrons reach the anode through the cusp sheaths; near-wall conductivity)
predeclared_hypotheses_from_the_audit.material_ordering: Al2O3 > BN in every effect (flux-averaged yields 0.82 vs 0.58 at 7 eV)
predeclared_hypotheses_from_the_audit.regime: with the Villemant BN fit the flux-averaged yield at the plateau T_e (5-7 eV) is 0.5-0.6 and the cusp-fed hot tail may reach the Hobbs-Wesson limit locally: the per-cell effective yield and the wall potential decide whether a cusp is classical, emitting or space-charge-limited - recorded, not tuned
predeclared_hypotheses_from_the_audit.status: hypotheses; a result of the opposite sign is a finding. The 100k-step box shakedown of this change is NOT a result (see the R2 report).

verification.unit: material anchors and identity (test_material_constants_...); yield curve reproduced statistically at 8 / 35 / 100 / 299 / 1500 eV and oblique incidence (5 sigma binomial), ion-induced yield; integer-yield sampling unbiased and clamped; emission distributions (elastic keeps the speed, cosine law <cos> = 2/3 and <cos^2> = 1/2, inelastic mean E/2, true secondaries mean 2 T_see and sd sqrt(2) T_see, BN 10 % backscattered); wall-crossing geometry on the bore and the cone stair with every emission point classified inside the plasma
verification.identities: particle-side energy identity to round-off with SEE on (cpu / warp-cpu / cuda), electron-count identity, surface charge = absorbed - emitted, extra keys outside the checkpoint key set; SEE-off identity / ledger keys / window sums / frame keys / fixed-run tallies pinned to v2.0.6
verification.warp: CUDA graph vs direct launches bitwise with SEE on (200 steps, ion-induced on); warp-cpu / cuda vs numpy reference in distribution (impacts, emitted, effective yield, backscattered fraction, mean emitted energy)
verification.physics_check: test_floating_dielectric_wall_sheath_drop_follows_hobbs_wesson_with_and_without_see: straight bore 2 mm (19 lambda_D), 24 x 64 cells, 2e16 m^-3 / 4 eV afterglow slab, grounded end plates, constant-yield model (threshold 3 eV, T_see 0.5 eV): delta 0 / 0.5 / 0.9 / 1.5 / 3.0 -> bulk-to-wall drop 11.09 / 9.83 / 7.41 / 3.61 / 3.11 V with T_e(delta = 0) 3.08 eV; the fall at equal time follows the Hobbs-Wesson factor T_e ln(1/(1 - delta_eff)) within 0.04 / 0.17 T_e (delta_eff 0.36 / 0.64 - the wall-defined yield, lower than delta because sub-threshold returning secondaries count as impacts); at delta 1.5 / 3.0 the effective yield saturates at 0.89 / 0.95 (< 1: the space-charge-limited state) and the drop is 1.17 / 1.01 T_e against the Hobbs-Wesson 1.02 T_e. Declared tolerances: strict monotone decrease; |difference - T_e ln(1/(1 - delta_eff))| <= 0.35 T_e; SCL drop in [0.7, 1.5] T_e with the two saturated cases within 25 %; effective yield in [0.8, 1); energy identity to 1e-9 of K_e. The ion-flux equilibrium value 5.27 T_e is not the test (it needs the ~1 us ion transit): the (1 - delta) factor and the SCL saturation are.
verification.box: H100 (extra MPS client): tests/pic2d CUDA modules; 100k-step shakedown of the reference 33 um protocol with SEE(BN) on through finalize + assess against the same-seed SEE-off run - an early direction reading, NOT a result (report)

see_dielectric_v1.cost: Warp: 3 launches + 1 scan per step (+3 on ion push steps when gamma_i > 0), one node-sized conversion; only flagged slots do work; ~+2-4 % per step expected (audit estimate) - measured on the box in the R2 report

unchanged_from_v2_0_6: every collision, neutral, cathode, field, pusher, deposition, Poisson (block-Thomas / device-mg), gate (peak-Debye window + accumulated floor, omega_pe dt on resolved nodes, windowed residual power, plume boundary), frame-recorder and checkpoint contract

the dielectric wall's field model: homogeneous Neumann (no conductance into solid cells) with the accumulated surface charge as the RHS source on the plasma-side wall nodes (audit gap (b) - permittivity / grounded backing - is NOT part of this change: in DC steady state the floating condition is the same; the charging transient and the tangential coupling near the exit lip remain declared simplifications)
recorded protocols carry no see block: their identities, resumes and replays are untouched
remaining_simplifications: no Hobbs-Wesson cap (by design: the space-charge-limited state emerges); a run whose cusps sit at or above the critical yield needs the per-cell effective yield read before any sheath-drop claim
no energy-dependent backscatter fractions beyond Sydorenko's constants; no elastic energy loss (Brandt's 90 %); no dependence of the emitted angular law on the incidence angle
Al2O3 constants are a declared bracket (Tondu 2011 curves not digitised); no aging / surface-conditioning model
ion-induced yield constant (no energy dependence); no sputtering / erosion
the dielectric is thick (Neumann) - gap (b) permittivity and backing are a separate change (audit 4.b)
